title: Low-precision variant intake API + nightly perf smoke harness
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Problem: currently low-precision variants (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) are onboarded via ad-hoc scripts and manual performance checks. There is no canonical intake API or nightly safety smoke that validates performance/accuracy delta against pinned FP16 baselines. This gap increases risk of silent regressions when model artifacts or quantization parameters change.

Goal: implement a variant intake API & manifest that normalizes metadata for precision variants, and a nightly smoke harness that runs a small but representative perf/quality suite and emits deterministic regression signals to the Console. The system should be lightweight (run on a small fleet nightly), actionable (clear metrics and thresholds), and gate candidate profile publishes until basic checks pass.

Scope: intake API (manifest schema + validation), artifact registry hooks, nightly CI job to run smoke workloads across INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ variants, regression detection rules, Console dashboard + alerting, and a small playbook for interpreting results.
acceptance_criteria: A manifest schema (JSON) for low-precision variant artifacts exists and is published in the docs with examples for INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ.
An HTTP ingestion endpoint (internal service) accepts a manifest and stores artifact metadata in the quant-variant registry; rejects malformed manifests with clear errors.

Nightly smoke job runs against all staged variants and measures latency (P50/P95), throughput, memory, and a compact quality suite (perplexity for LLMs, embedding cosine drift for embedding models) against the pinned FP16 baseline.

Regression detection rules implemented: fail if P95 latency regresses >15% AND absolute P95 > 150ms, or quality metric delta exceeds configured thresholds (e.g., perplexity increase >1.0 or embedding cosine drop >0.01).
Console shows a per-variant nightly report and creates an alert channel when a variant fails the smoke checks.
tasks: Define manifest fields: model_id, model_version, quant_backend, quant_config_hash, sample_sequence_distribution, testset_id, pinned_fp16_baseline, artifacts_uri, signer_id, created_by
Implement ingestion endpoint and validation lib (Node + Typescript) with unit tests
Wire ingestion to quant-variant registry (add DB table + indices)
Create compact nightly smoke harness (containerized) that pulls variants, runs a small workload (100 short prompts + 50 long prompts) and collects latency/kv cache behavior and quality metrics
Implement regression detection rules and a lightweight statistical smoothing to reduce flakiness (rolling-3-night median)
Add Console dashboard tile and PagerDuty/Slack alert integration for failed variants
Draft runbook for triage and rollback/pinning guidance
Add CI gate: block publish of variant to public catalog if nightly smoke fails for two consecutive runs
updates: 2025-09-11: Kickoff design sync with Runtime, DevInfra, and Console teams. Agreed to reuse existing artifact signing pattern from ENG-21803.
2025-09-12: Prototype manifest schema v0.1 posted to Google Drive (link below). Decided to include sample_sequence_distribution to support kernel tuning.
2025-09-15: Spike completed for a minimal harness that runs on dev GPU pool. Initial false positive rate ~12% due to variance on noisy hosts — plan to add rolling median and minimal warmup runs.
2025-09-17: Design review with PM and Security. Security requested explicit signer_id and KMS-backed signature validation for artifact publish; added to manifest requirements.
risk_and_mitigations: False positives due to noisy infra: mitigate via rolling-3-night median + minimum sample size + warmup requests
Cost of nightly runs at scale: run compact representative subset (10% of full eval) and prioritize variants in staging buckets
Over-blocking deploys: require two consecutive nightly failures to block publish; provide fast manual override for urgent security fixes
Stale testset drift: rotate small canonical testset quarterly and track testset drift metric
notes: Tradeoffs considered: full eval per variant (expensive & slow) vs compact nightly smoke (cheap but less sensitive). We chose compact nightly with conservative thresholds and can opt into full eval on-demand.
We will canonicalize quant_config_hash to ensure deterministic identity for a variant (helps pinning and reproduceability).
Plan to reuse the unified artifact format work (ENG-21803) but add quant-specific fields and signer metadata.
